title: Navier–Stokes — Clay Millennium challenge (A/B/C/D)
statement: Prove at least one of Clay alternatives A, B, C or D; these are alternatives, not an AND-decomposition. A/B concern unforced global smooth existence on R3/T3; C/D permit admissible smooth forcing in a breakdown example. OpenAI reports C and D; Clay acknowledged apparent settlement on 2026-09-11. Resolution reported, awaiting this graph’s independent proof and theorem-correspondence review; no prize award is recorded.

criteria.test: Prove global smooth bounded-energy solutions for all smooth divergence-free data satisfying Clay (4), with f=0 on R3; equations (1)-(3), (6)-(7).
Prove global smooth spatially periodic velocity and pressure for all smooth divergence-free periodic initial data, with f=0 on T3; Clay (8), (10)-(11) and pressure-periodicity erratum.
Exhibit smooth divergence-free initial data and smooth forcing satisfying Clay (4)-(5) on R3 for which no global smooth uniformly bounded-energy solution exists.
Exhibit smooth divergence-free periodic initial data and smooth forcing satisfying Clay (8)-(9) for which no global smooth periodic solution exists on T3.

title: Navier–Stokes breakdown — smooth forcing, whole space (Clay C)
statement: Can admissible smooth forcing and smooth divergence-free initial data produce finite-time breakdown for 3-D incompressible Navier–Stokes on R3 with positive viscosity? OpenAI’s Theorem 1.1 reports a construction starting from rest with smooth compactly supported forcing and uniformly bounded kinetic energy before blowup. It does not settle the unforced problem. Reported resolution; independent review not recorded here.

title: Navier–Stokes breakdown — smooth forcing, periodic domain (Clay D)
statement: Can admissible smooth periodic forcing and smooth divergence-free periodic data cause breakdown for 3-D incompressible Navier–Stokes with positive viscosity on T3? OpenAI reports the periodic construction in Corollary 10.6. This is a distinct domain from the whole-space case and does not settle unforced periodic regularity. Reported resolution; independent review not recorded here.

statement: For 3-D incompressible Navier–Stokes with positive viscosity on T3 and zero external forcing, do smooth divergence-free periodic initial data always admit global smooth periodic velocity and pressure? The announced forced C/D results do not settle this question.

title: Euler finite-time breakdown — unforced, whole space
statement: Can smooth compactly supported divergence-free initial velocity for 3-D incompressible Euler on R3 develop a finite-time singularity without external forcing? OpenAI reports such a construction, with unbounded velocity gradient and divergent time-integrated supremum vorticity. This inviscid result does not establish unforced viscous Navier–Stokes breakdown. Reported resolution; independent review not recorded here.
